What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0033-0012 at 12:15 on 2023-01-05 found crude oil on the pad: about 7.9% of the pad area, estimated 4.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 5.6 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0033-012

Asset: WELL-0033 (SW-23 Well 033, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: rod string Work started: 14 Jul 2024 08:00 · Finished: 30 Jul 2024 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 384 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0033-0091 on 2024-07-11 Report written: 31 Jul 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0033-0091 showed the wellhead at 48.1 °C with the air at 37.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 14 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0033-0207 showed the wellhead at 27.4 °C with the air at 26.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass.
